newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIAN TARTU BREWER OPTIMISTIC AFTER OLVI MOVE.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIAN TARTU BREWER OPTIMISTIC AFTER OLVI MOVE.

text.p: Estonian brewer ~Tartu Olletehas~, signing a deal to sell 15 percent of its shares to Finland's Olvi , said it would boost its exports via Olvi and become the best brewer in the Baltics.

Olvi is encroaching on a Baltic market which has so far been the preserve of Baltic Beverage Holding, a joint venture between Hartwall and Pripps Ringnes, owned by Norwegian food conglomerate Orkla and Volvo .
Olvi paid 10 million kroons for the shares, officials said.
It also said it wanted to put at least a quarter of its shares onto the burgeoning Tallinn stock exchange.
"Our strategy is essentially to increase our exports using the Olvi network," Tartu marketing director Arho Anttilia told a news conference.
"Our aim is to become the best brewery in the Baltic states and the CIS countries," he added.
Tartu Olletehas had share capital of 7.5 million kroons and turnover last year of 175 million kroons.
The brewer is owned by Magnum Konsumer, which is also the main stakeholder in the Tallinn Pharmaceutical>company, which recently sold 10 percent of its shares to foreign investors.
"Both parties have agreed that next year 25 percent of Tartu shares will be listed on the Tallinn stock exchange," Magnum Konsumer representative Margus Linnemae said.
